items.summary: Abdul El-Sayed (D) and Mike Rogers (R) meet tonight, Oct 21, at 7 PM ET in the WXYZ-TV Detroit studios for their second and final scheduled debate in the open Michigan Senate seat, after their fiery Oct 8 face-off at WOOD-TV in Grand Rapids; moderated by editorial director Chuck Stokes with anchors Carolyn Clifford and Alicia Smith, livestreamed on freep.com/WXYZ. El-Sayed leads the RCP polling average ~+2.6 (Marist 50-48, Oct 21). Also confirmed: Trump's Oct 25 Port Huron rally for Rogers (McMorran Place Arena, doors 11:30 AM, remarks 3 PM) — the first-ever sitting-president visit to St. Clair County, a day after Obama's Oct 24 Detroit rally with El-Sayed. This feed previously held the Oct 25 rally as unconfirmed; it is now confirmed by the Port Huron Times Herald and the Free Press.
items.title: Michigan Senate final debate tonight (7 PM, WXYZ); Trump Oct 25 Port Huron rally confirmed

items.event_time_ist: Rally 7 PM ET, Oct 21 (4:30 AM IST, Oct 22); Graham AP interview Sat, Oct 17; Trafalgar fielded Oct 18-19
items.summary: Trump rallies at Clemson's T. Ed Garrison Arena tonight, Oct 21 (doors 3:30 PM, remarks ~7 PM ET) for Sen. Darline Graham, who is 'running about even' with Democrat Annie Andrews in a state Trump won by ~18 points; nonpartisan analysts rate SC Likely R or Lean R. The rally lands amid a visible GOP rift: Trump last week waived sanctions under the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act (her late brother's bill); Graham told AP on Sat Oct 17 she would 'choose to keep the pressure on Russia... I don't trust Putin, and I don't trust Russia.' Sen. Cornyn: 'Lindsey would be appalled'; Sen. Tillis called the waiver 'beyond irresponsible' (TIME); Zelensky called it 'unfortunate.' Fresh SC polls: Trafalgar (R, Oct 18-19) has Graham 49-46 Andrews; Decision Desk HQ polling average (Oct 18): Graham 46.2-43.9 (+2.3), a statistical tie. Clemson College Democrats are protesting 2:30-5 PM at the venue entrance.
items.title: Trump's Clemson rally tonight amid GOP rift over Russia sanctions waiver; SC Senate a statistical tie

items.summary: AJC/UGA SPIA poll (1,000 likely voters, telephone, Oct 7-15, MoE ±3.1), released Oct 21: Sen. Jon Ossoff (D) 48%, Rep. Mike Collins (R) 40%, 12% undecided — lead outside the margin of error; Ossoff job approval 55%. Ossoff leads among women, Black voters, young voters, and college grads; Collins leads among white voters, voters 65+, and non-college voters. The same poll found the GA governor race tied (Jackson 46, Bottoms 45 — reported Oct 20). Second pollster: Quantus Insights (Oct 15-17): Ossoff 51.8-44.9; RCP average now Ossoff +8.5. Watch GA's 50% runoff threshold — Ossoff sits just under it.
items.title: AJC poll: Ossoff leads Collins 48-40 in Georgia Senate race
